name: Shatyly Panorama
near: Bokonbaevo is ~12 km west of the start of the trail (Lonely Planet: 12 km east of the roundabout in the center of the village; Asia Hikes: 11.5 km along the Boz-Salkyn valley). Kadji-Sai is closer in a straight line, but the approach is described only from Bokonbaevo.
elev: The viewpoint is ~2,600 m, the start ~2,490 m per the Wikiloc GPS track (max. 8,588 ft / min. 8,155 ft, recorded May 2017); gain 137–177 m (Wikiloc/Asia Hikes). Accuracy ±50 m; there is no official elevation mark.
short: An easy one-hour walk from the Boz-Salkyn valley to a grassy hill with a panorama of the whole southern shore of Issyk-Kul, the lake itself and the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges; the best place for sunrise near Bokonbaevo.
desc: Shatyly is a viewing ridge above the Boz-Salkyn valley in the foothills of the Terskey Ala-Too, east of Bokonbaevo. From a farm at a bend in the dirt road a jeep track climbs to a northern saddle, from which a short climb to the left leads to a lookout hill. The 3.5 km loop with a gain of under 200 m takes about an hour; the trail has no water or shade. From the top you can see the lake in its full width, the barren hills of the shore, the settlement of Kadji-Sai and snowy peaks. The name of the valley, “Boz-Salkyn” (“light coolness”), became established after the film of the same name and does not appear on topographic maps. The route is promoted by CBT/Destination South Shore as a “morning or half-day” outing from Bokonbaevo; there is no entry fee. Combined with the Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Manjyly-Ata and the eagle-hunter (berkutchi) show, it makes a standard day on the southern shore.
guide: Come for sunrise: the sun rises behind the ridge and paints the lake and hills orange — that is what people come here for. Leave Bokonbaevo before dawn, 12 km of dirt road to the farm at the bend, then along the jeep track to the saddle and left to the hill — all in 30–40 minutes. There is no water or shade on the trail, and the wind on the ridge is strong, so take a jacket and a thermos. If you have no car, arrange a taxi at CBT Bokonbaevo or walk the 18 km from the village (that is another +3 hours). Combine it with Skazka Canyon and the Manjyly-Ata springs — everything is within half an hour’s drive.
see: The panorama of the whole lake and the southern shore; the Boz-Salkyn valley with summer pastures; at sunrise — light on the barren hills; views of Kadji-Sai and the Terskey Ala-Too. Nearby — the Mars canyons (6 km), the Manjyly-Ata valley (7 km), Skazka Canyon (23 km).
skip: What matters to you is the route itself, not the view — it is only 1 hour of walking here. The weather is overcast or hazy: the point of this spot is the panorama. You have no car and are not ready to pay for a round-trip taxi for an hour’s walk.
diff: Very easy: a 3.5 km loop, gain 137–177 m, under an hour (Asia Hikes 2021, Wikiloc 2017). No water or shade; suitable for children in dry weather.
when: May–October; in summer — only the morning because of the heat on the open slope. In spring (May) the hills are green, in autumn the air is clear. In winter access along the dirt road depends on the snow.
hours: Open terrain, 24 hours; no ticket offices or barriers (Asia Hikes 2021: no fee).
daytime: Sunrise (Lonely Planet, Journal of Nomads 2025: “worth arriving before sunrise”); in the evening — sunset with the lake lit up, but you have to return along the dirt road in the dark.
how: From Bokonbaevo: from the central roundabout two blocks south, then the road east out of the village, 12 km along the Boz-Salkyn valley to a small farm at a bend in the road; then on foot along the jeep track to the saddle and left to the hill (~1.75 km one way). On foot from Bokonbaevo — +18 km/3 h. To Bokonbaevo: a marshrutka (minibus) from Bishkek (Bishkek bus station, 1/1 Alma-Atinskaya St., 550–650 som, 5–6 h, every 1–2 h from 7:00 to 17:00 — Journal of Nomads, 2025) or from Karakol (1.5–2 h).
needcar: Yes, to the start of the trail (12 km of dirt road from the village); on site — on foot. A taxi from Bokonbaevo or a transfer through CBT.
self: Yes: the trail is obvious (a jeep track), GPS tracks on Wikiloc/AllTrails, no permits or fees.
roadtype: Paved only in Bokonbaevo; 12 km is a dirt village road along the valley (passable for a passenger car in dry weather, Asia Hikes: “old mountain roads”, a taxi or hitchhiking); then a jeep track on foot.
traveltime: Bokonbaevo – trailhead: 20–30 min by car (12 km of dirt road). The climb to the viewpoint is 30–40 min, the loop about an hour (Asia Hikes, Owl Over The World 2024).
stay: In Bokonbaevo: the guesthouses Baiel, Akbermet (budget), Amirhan, Ecoresort Kaiyrma (mid-range) — Journal of Nomads 2025; Guest House Teskei (Owl Over The World 2024); 4 CBT Bokonbaevo yurt camps from the shore to the foothills. Prices are not published (a regional guideline of 1,000–2,000 som/person with breakfast — not confirmed).
net: In Bokonbaevo and Kadji-Sai — coverage from all operators (a district center, the A363 highway). On the Shatyly ridge coverage is not documented; given the remoteness (12 km from the village, line of sight to the shore) a signal is likely but not confirmed.
entry: Free — there is no entry fee (Asia Hikes, 2021). No recent data on the introduction of a fee was found.
transfer: A taxi in Bokonbaevo to the start — the tariff is not published (a guideline of 500–1,000 som round trip, not confirmed). Marshrutka Bishkek – Bokonbaevo 550–650 som, shared taxi 800–1,000 som/seat, a whole car 3,500–4,000 som (2025).
bring: Water (there are no springs on the trail), a hat and sun protection, a windbreaker for the ridge, a flashlight if you set out before dawn, a camera; shoes with a tread — the slopes are loose.
warn: No water or shade — it is hot in the daytime in summer. The dirt road turns to mud after rain. Shepherd dogs at the farms in the valley — give them a wide berth. The name “Boz-Salkyn” is absent from maps — navigate by the GPS track, not by the place name.
food: There is nothing on site. In Bokonbaevo — the Argymak café (the CBT address, 16 Mambetov St.), home cooking at guesthouses; on the southern shore — smoked fish and kumis by the highway (seasonal). Specific establishments have not been checked.
reviews: Google Maps “Panorama Shatyly Issyk-Kul”: 4.9/5, 29 ratings (03.10.2026). AllTrails “Shatyly Overlook”: 9 reviews (content unavailable). Blogs 2021–2025 are unanimous: an easy climb, the best views at sunrise; cons — you need transport to the start, no water.
p.sum: Stay overnight in Bokonbaevo and set out by taxi or your own car before dawn: 12 km of village dirt road along the Boz-Salkyn valley to the farm at the bend, then 1.75 km on foot along the jeep track to the hill — in time for sunrise. Entry is free, and there is no water or shade. Without a car, arrange a taxi through CBT Bokonbaevo or a guesthouse; it combines conveniently into one day with Manjyly-Ata and the Mars and Skazka canyons.

p.iti.0.title: Sunrise + the southern shore in a day
p.iti.0.plan: 4:30–5:00 leave Bokonbaevo → sunrise at Shatyly → 8:00 breakfast at a guesthouse → 9:30 Manjyly-Ata (springs, 1.5–2 h) → Mars canyons → lunch in Kadji-Sai → Skazka Canyon closer to sunset.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days on the southern shore
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek → Bokonbaevo (5–6 h), the eagle-hunter show, a night in a yurt camp. Day 2: Shatyly at sunrise → Manjyly-Ata → Skazka → Barskoon or Karakol.
p.iti.2.title: Combining stops along the route
p.iti.2.plan: Shatyly → Manjyly-Ata (8–10 km) → Mars canyons → Kadji-Sai → Skazka (~30 km) → Barskoon (waterfalls, Arabel).
p.season: April–May — green hills, mud after rain; June–August — sunrise only (heat, no shade), beach season on the shore; September–October — clear air, the best views; in winter — access over snow, cold wind. No crowds.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka Bishkek – Bokonbaevo 550–650; guesthouse ~1,000–1,500 with breakfast; taxi to the start ~500–1,000 per car (÷ among the group); entry free. ≈ 2,000–3,000 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Shared taxi 800–1,000 or a car 3,500–4,000; yurt camp/eco-resort ~2,000–4,000; guide/horseback ride via CBT. ≈ 5,000–8,000 som/person.
p.permits: Not needed; no fee (Asia Hikes 2021, no recent fees found).
p.access: With children — yes (a short climb, in dry weather); for older people — doable at a slow pace, the slope is loose; stroller — no; dog — allowed, but be careful with shepherd dogs at the farms.
